title: Half-Life and Radioactive Dating
learningObjectives: Explain half-life as the time required for exactly one-half of parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms
Use measurements of remaining parent atoms and produced daughter atoms to compute the numeric age of a rock in years

sources.title: Fossils, Rocks, and Time: The Numeric Time Scale — U.S. Geological Survey

evidence.quote: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is the length of time required for exactly one-half of the parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms.
The change from parent to daughter happens at a constant rate, called the half-life.

explanations.text: Half-life is the constant rate of decay: the time required for exactly one-half of parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms.

evidence.quote: A radioactive isotope (the parent) of one chemical element naturally converts to a stable isotope (the daughter)

explanations.text: A radioactive parent isotope naturally converts to a stable daughter isotope of another element by changes in the nucleus.

evidence.quote: Now we can use minerals that contain naturally occurring radioactive elements to calculate the numeric age of a rock in years.
measurements of the number of remaining atoms of the parent and the number of atoms of the new daughter produced

explanations.text: Minerals with radioactive elements can be used to calculate numeric rock age in years by measuring remaining parent atoms and produced daughter atoms.

predictions.prompt: A 100-gram sample has a half-life of 5 years. How much remains after 5 years?
A 200-gram sample has a half-life of 8 years. How much remains after 12 years?
